## Intent
Hypothesis: compiler auto-vectorization over per-particle components can approach the streaming ceiling on death-free workloads.

## Cache saturation
At q=0.01, ns/p falls from 11.908 (N=4000) to 8.055 (N=16000) — overhead amortization at small N. All measured points are past the L1d spill (N≈949). The L2 spill at N≈60787 falls between N=16000 and N=65000; cost stays FLAT across it (8.055→7.904 ns/p), no knee. From N=65000 through N=4000000, cost remains FLAT at ~8.0 ns/p. Death rate raises the floor — q=0.25 sits at ~10.0 ns/p vs ~8.0 at q=0.01 — without changing the N-shape: still falls from small N, still flat through L2→DRAM. No spill knee at any death rate confirms the algo is not bandwidth-limited.

## Bandwidth
Peak is 8.73 GB/s at N=65000, q=0.01 — 34.6% of the 25.22 GB/s ceiling. At q=0.25 it drops to 6.89 GB/s (27.3%) and stays flat for N≥65000. Overhead-bound at small N (5.06–5.97 GB/s at N=4000); compute/overhead-bound at large N — never bandwidth-bound, plateauing far below ceiling with no bandwidth-limited regime. Death rate transitions the floor: q≤0.05 holds 8.4–8.7 GB/s, q=0.25 collapses to ~6.9 GB/s, driven by the branchy respawn scan.

## Assembly
The compiler vectorized across components of one particle, not across particles. The core loop loads fields with `ldur q1` (4 floats) + `ldr d2` (2 floats), rearranges via `ext.16b v3, v1, v2, #0xc`, inserts a scalar with `mov.s v3[3], v0[0]`, then runs `fmul.4s v0, v3, v4` / `fadd.4s v0, v1, v0` — 4-lane SIMD on one particle. A gather appears: `ld1.s {v2}[1], [x8]` loads one indexed float into a lane. Walk2's respawn scan is entirely scalar: 35 `bl` calls to `_layouts.ML01.data.Data.spawn`, each guarded by `ldrb`+`cbz`, with byte-granular `strb` stores — explaining why death rate raises the floor without changing the N-shape. Component-wise vec on stride-69 data with a gather caps bandwidth at 35% of ceiling.

## Verdict
Refuted — at q=0.01 the algo sustains 8.73 GB/s = 34.6% of the 25.22 GB/s ceiling with no cache-spill knee, confirming component-wise auto-vectorization with a `ld1.s` gather cannot approach streaming even near death-free. Death rate raises the floor from 8.0 to 10.0 ns/p (q=0.01→0.25) via the 35-call scalar respawn scan, but the flat N-shape at all death rates confirms the bottleneck is compute and gather overhead, not bandwidth.
